newsitem.title: USA: KIWI fails to get financing ok, to end flights.
newsitem.headline: KIWI fails to get financing ok, to end flights.

text.p: Kiwi International Air Lines said on Tuesday it would suspend flights Tuesday night, after failing earlier in the day to get its financing proposal approved to continue operating.

The company said it had interest from several investors, including a $2 million proposal from Remington Products Co owner Victor Kiam II, but no firm offer materialized during the hearing in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Newark, N.J., the company said.
"No one wanted to pony up, and the last-minute Hail Mary pass to Victor Kiam was dropped in the end zone," said company spokesman Rob Kulat.
The 1,200-employee company had $40 million in debt and declared bankruptcy September 30. After filing bankruptcy it had cut its schedule back from 63 daily flights to 24.

The airlines said it had started building profitability in the first half of 1996, but that it was hurt by the ValuJet crash and a partial shutdown by the Federal Aviation Administration in June to resolve record-keeping issues with its pilot training program.
It had sought to secure at least $5 million in debtor-in-possession financing as part of its reorganization.
According to a bankruptcy court clerk, the carrier is scheduled to go court again October 22. According to the clerk the carrier has $35 million in assets and $55 million in liabilities.
